Samira: Heads-up — customer `finops-inc` opened a support case: p99 latency on text.generate jumped ~2x starting ~04:10 UTC. They report billing alerts firing due to token timeouts. Escalating to eng-runtime.
Ashwin: Copy. Any correlation with recent kernel/compile flag rollout?
Samira: Customer included trace snippet: 2026-03-17T04:11:02Z request id=abc123 p99=980ms, baseline ~420ms. No auth/billing errors, just massive tail.
Kevin: sre-bot shows a small bump in p95/p99 for hosted region eu-west-1 around 04:08. Deployments?
sre-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout `kernelselect-v2` completed 03:55 UTC -> stable 04:00 UTC. Metric anomalies pushed at 04:07.
Marta: That rollout toggles new priority hop for kernel selection (prefer-flash true + compile-flag X). Could be our heuristic mis-routing longer sequences to FlashAttention variant which regresses on certain seq/batch mixes.
Ashwin: Repro attempt: running local perf harness w/seed loadprofile from finops. Command: ```./perf_runner --model gpt-medium --seq 512 --batch 8 --kernel flash --warmup 20 --iters 200``` Observed p99 950ms, p95 410ms. When I switch kernel=sdpa p99 430ms.
Ashwin: So FlashAttention->SDPA fallback reduces tail. Suspect the compile flag added in v2 made flash slower on medium batch variance.
Kevin: Immediate mitigation: rollback kernel_selector to previous stable policy or force route finops customer to sdpa variant. Which is faster to push?
Marta: For a quick fix we can set a routing override for finops tenant to prefer_sdpa. That's a one-line change in routing service and doesn't touch runtime. I can push that right now.
Samira: Customer asked for ETA. If you can do the override within 10 min, they want status update.
Opsina: I'll apply the override and notify. Patching route: ```POST /admin/routes/override {"tenant":"finops-inc","kernel_preference":"sdpa"}``` -> applied.
support-bot: Noted. Customer notified: "We routed you to fallback kernel variant while we investigate."
Ashwin: After override the synthetic test shows p99 back to ~430ms for finops profile. Good.
Kevin: Next steps: reproduce root cause, narrow to compile flag or kernel priority heuristic. Ashwin, can you run perf with FlashAttention but previous compile flags? We should test toggling -fno-fast-math-like flags or kernel-specific defines.
Ashwin: On it. Quick diff in build: removed flag `-DENABLE_V2_KERNEL_OPT` and recompiled flash kernel. Re-run harness -> p99 440ms. With flag enabled -> p99 940ms. So it's that flag interacting with certain microkernel path.
Marta: Great repro. Can we make the flag conditional on sequence length distribution? Maybe the heuristic incorrectly prefers the v2 opt for seqs >256 but workload has many short/long mixes and that causes cache thrash.
Kevin: Short term: keep tenant override + pin rollout to v1 until we have a fix. Medium term: add a canary that measures p99 on seq buckets and auto-backout if regressions >20%.
Ashwin: I'll open PR to gate ENABLE_V2_KERNEL_OPT behind a runtime flag and add a test in kerneltuner that runs perf buckets during canary. PR: https://repo/rdw/kerneltuner/pull/482
Marta: Also add a quick mitigation playbook entry: steps to route tenant, rollback compile flag via feature flag, and recompile safe binary. Put in runbook under eng-runtime/incidents.
Kevin: Assigning followups: Ashwin - PR + unit canary tests. Marta - runbook + postmortem draft. Opsina - coordinate with support to confirm customer SLA effects. Samira - keep customer loop updated.
Samira: Customer acknowledges rollback and is seeing improved tail. They want quarterly postmortem. Will coordinate.
Kevin: Good recovery. Reminder: next rollout should include seq-split p99 check in release pipeline.
Marta: Noted. Also leaving a note to re-evaluate compile-flag heuristic — it speeds median tokens but harms tail for mixed-batch workloads.
Ashwin: Filed issue with microkernel vendor about unexpected performance cliff when ENABLE_V2_KERNEL_OPT is on for certain CUDA driver versions. Link in PR.
support-bot: Incident resolved for tenant finops-inc, mitigation applied. Closing message to customer queued.
Kevin: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread pinned to the rollout ticket and postmortem. :thumbsup:
